## Course code and lab starters

Use this website as the primary source for course reading. To clone the code,
synthetic data, and lab starters, use the public GitHub repository:

<https://github.com/slzhao/BIOS6301-materials>
:::

## Start here

1. Complete [Session 0](course/session00/index.qmd) before the first class.
2. Read the [course syllabus](syllabus.qmd).
3. In Session 2, set up separate course-materials and personal-work projects.
4. Pull the course clone before class; copy starters into your personal repository.

## Course sequence

| Session | Topic | Main emphasis |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | [Setup and orientation](course/session00/index.qmd) | self-study diagnostic |
| 1 | [Reproducible documents and workflow](course/session01/index.qmd) | RStudio, R Markdown, and Quarto |
| 2 | [Git and GitHub](course/session02/index.qmd) | version control |
| 3 | [R objects](course/session03/index.qmd) | base R foundations |
| 4 | [Data structures and base-R handling](course/session04/index.qmd) | containers and base R |
| 5 | [Getting data into R](course/session05/index.qmd) | files, checks, and dates |
| 6 | [Tidy data and dplyr](course/session06/index.qmd) | tidyverse + base verification |
| 7 | [Reshaping and joins](course/session07/index.qmd) | relational data |
| 8 | [Visualization](course/session08/index.qmd) | base graphics + ggplot2 |
| 9 | [Positron and AI-assisted coding](course/session09/index.qmd) | Copilot verification and policy |
| 10 | [Python introduction for R users](course/session10/index.qmd) | translation from familiar R |
| 11 | [Control flow and functions](course/session11/index.qmd) | base R programming |
| 12 | [Debugging and numerical reliability](course/session12/index.qmd) | reliable code |
| 13 | [Iteration, vectorization, and functionals](course/session13/index.qmd) | loops, base functionals, and purrr |
| 14 | [Random generation and simulation](course/session14/index.qmd) | Monte Carlo studies |
| 15 | [Resampling](course/session15/index.qmd) | bootstrap, permutation, CV |
| 16 | [Selected Practical Topics in R](course/session16/index.qmd) | strings, regex, and flexible needs |

## R dialect policy

Base R and tidyverse are both accepted. Some sessions target a specific tool for
learning, but otherwise choose the style that makes the data meaning and checks
easiest to audit. You should be able to read both and verify important results.

## Repository boundary

Keep two separate repositories beside each other:

```text
BIOS6301-materials/   read, copy, and Pull before class; leave files unchanged
BIOS6301-mywork/      your private project; edit and Commit work/ here
```

Open `BIOS6301-materials.Rproj` and click **Pull** before each class.
Then open `BIOS6301-mywork.Rproj` to edit copied lab files and homework.
Your personal repository contains your own work and requires no instructor
remote or course history. Follow the [Session 2 lab](course/session02/lab.qmd)
for setup.

Do not place credentials or restricted research data in either repository.
